channel.title: AgentScout
channel.description: Latest AI agent tools and agent news from AgentScout.

item.title: AskSolique
item.description: AskSolique is an AI research workspace for India tax and company law. It answers from primary sources across income tax, GST, FEMA, corporate law, SEBI and customs, and it can turn that research into a deliverable. Browsing the regulatory library costs 0 credits. A 7-day trial needs no card. Paid use, quoted exclusive of GST on 20 Nov 2026, is a pack at ₹999 for 4,000 credits or ₹3,999 a month for 16,000 credits.

item.title: Bitpont
item.description: Bitpont is an onchain finance app for swaps, bridges, derivatives and earn positions, with a remote MCP for agents at https://www.bitpont.com/api/v1/mcp. The agent guides say a public read needs no API key, and a trade is signed by the agent's own wallet rather than by handing Bitpont the keys. Setup notes are at https://www.bitpont.com/help/ai-agents/ and the developer docs are at https://www.bitpont.com/developers/.

item.title: AI Rap Video Forge
item.description: AI Rap Video Forge builds a short rap video from two photos and a prompt, on templates such as a studio, a neon street, a rooftop or a pet performance. You confirm you are 18 or older and have permission to use the photos. On 20 Nov 2026 the pricing page listed Basic at $9.90 for 30 credits, Pro at $19.90 for 70 credits and Studio at $29.90 for 110 credits. A 5-second clip is 10 credits, 10 seconds is 20 and 15 seconds is 30. Credits do not expire, and failed videos return them.

item.title: imageat
item.description: imageat is an agentic studio for photos and video: you pick a model, edit on one canvas, and can call the same credits from an MCP connector or an API. Sign-up is free. On 20 Nov 2026 the pricing page showed monthly image allowances of 10, 30 and 100 on the tiers it displayed, with the MCP connector billed to an API balance. Dollar amounts on that page were not a single clean rate card, so they are not repeated here.

item.title: VideoEnhancer
item.description: VideoEnhancer upscales video in the browser with FlashVSR to 1080p, 2K or 4K, and uses Real-ESRGAN for still images. A 5-second trial is free; longer processing is paid. Video HD accepts MP4 up to 120 seconds and 500 MB, with no watermark. On 20 Nov 2026 the pricing page listed Basic at $19.90 a month for 1,660 credits ($0.012 a credit) and Premium at $39.90 a month for 4,000 credits ($0.01 a credit). One-time packs start at $30 for 1,000 credits.

item.title: APT Video AI
item.description: APT Video AI makes a short music video from two photos on a fixed pink-studio template: one person at the drums, one singing, with the template audio already in the file. A clip is about 13 seconds in landscape or portrait and costs 26 credits. The page says $9.90 is two videos, paid once, with no subscription. Photos are described as staying on the device until you sign in.

item.title: NextlerAI
item.description: NextlerAI builds a website, a web app or an iOS and Android app from a short description of the business and what a visitor should do. The public page, in Estonian and English, starts from example projects such as a menu, a portfolio or an event page, and the English description says you start with a free account. No dollar price was on the page on 20 Nov 2026.

item.title: Valmera
item.description: Valmera is an AI video editor that turns a long talk or podcast into a short with captions, reframing and music, then exports an MP4. The same paid plans include a hosted MCP so Claude, ChatGPT or Cursor can drive the edit. The MCP page is https://valmera.io/mcp and the connector repo is ABO3SKRALMASAOODI/valmera-mcp. On 20 Nov 2026 Plus was $15 a month (500 credits), Pro $50 (1,500 credits) and Max $100 (4,000 credits). Annual billing is ten months' price for twelve: $150, $500 or $1,000. Example exports on the homepage carry a free-tier watermark.

item.title: TianDun
item.description: TianDun is a video studio from Quanzhou TianDun Intelligent Things Tech that chains a brief, a template, images, speech, avatars and video into one plan. The English page lets you browse without an account and asks you to sign in to generate. A product-ad template is marked from about 1.2 credits, failed jobs are refunded, and credits are recharged in the app. No dollar price was on that page on 20 Nov 2026.

item.title: Nowah
item.description: Nowah is an AI travel agent for iPhone and Android. You describe a trip, paste a short-video link, or name a budget, and it proposes flights with live fares, builds an itinerary, and books only after you confirm and pay. It also tracks prices, checks visas and sells eSIMs. On 20 Nov 2026 Nowah Pro Monthly was $24.99 a month, and Pro Yearly was $79 for the first year, then $199 a year.

item.title: Kruqond
item.description: Kruqond is an AI search engine that queries public web pages, social posts, comments, video and code and returns cited results. The homepage offers 5 free searches with no sign-up. On 20 Nov 2026 the pricing page listed a monthly plan at $19 for 50 credits and an annual plan at $15 a month, billed $180 a year, for 700 credits.

item.title: Twitch Emote Maker
item.description: Twitch Emote Maker, from Emote Studio, turns a text idea or a photo into a Twitch emote and previews it at 112, 56 and 28 pixels. Static emotes cost 30 credits and animated GIFs cost 80. On 20 Nov 2026 the pricing page sold a Starter pack at $5.99 for 250 credits, as one-time packs with no subscription. Failed generations return the credits. Sample files can be previewed before you buy.

item.title: AI Picture Checker
item.description: AI Picture Checker uploads a JPG, PNG or WebP, up to 20 MB, and returns a verdict on whether the picture looks AI-generated, with a confidence score and sometimes a guess at the source model. The site's FAQ says free checks have a daily limit and the checker shows how many are left. A specific daily number was not in the page source on 20 Nov 2026, so this listing does not state one.

item.title: TOON
item.description: TOON (Token-Oriented Object Notation) is an MIT format for putting the JSON data model into an LLM prompt in fewer tokens. The project ships a spec, a CLI and implementations. Its own benchmark, published on toonformat.dev, says retrieval accuracy stays close to JSON (72.2% versus 71.4%) at 42.6% fewer tokens. GitHub listed 25,641 stars on toon-format/toon on 20 Nov 2026.

item.title: Plurai
item.description: Plurai is a simulation and post-training layer that runs an agent through scenarios so later runs get sharper. The homepage shows a plugin install for Claude Code, GitHub Copilot CLI, OpenAI Codex and Cursor. Hosted use is offered through a demo rather than a public rate card, so this listing does not state a price.

item.title: Creatify
item.description: Creatify generates image and video ads from a product URL, including avatar spots and ad variations, and its product navigation includes an MCP integration. The homepage says you can try it for free. The pricing page lists credit plans; the struck monthly and annual figures were not clear enough to quote, so this listing does not state a dollar price.

item.title: APIPod
item.description: APIPod is one API, and a remote MCP, for image and video models from several providers. The site says you pay as you go, with no subscription, and you can start for free. It documents the MCP at https://api.apipod.ai/mcp for Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor and Codex.

item.title: inference.sh
item.description: inference.sh is a single API for running image, video, audio, text, search and 3D models, plus a skill registry and a path from a demo agent to a durable one with a person in the loop. It is listed in the official MCP registry. The homepage on 20 Nov 2026 did not show a rate card, so this listing does not state a price.

item.title: AgenticCart
item.description: AgenticCart makes a store's catalog findable and buyable inside ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and other agents, without a second checkout. The homepage on 20 Nov 2026 offered a 7-day free trial that you can cancel.

item.title: AdStar
item.description: AdStar turns a product into video ads and connects to the assistants people already use, including ChatGPT, Claude, Claude Code, Codex and Cursor. The homepage, checked 20 Nov 2026, did not publish a price, so this listing does not state one.

item.title: OpenAI starts testing always-on Dots agents on the $20 Plus plan
item.description: The Verge reports OpenAI is testing its always-on Dots agents with a small number of $20 ChatGPT Plus subscribers. Dots had been limited to Pro and higher tiers, and they are also rolling out to every ChatGPT Business Standard user.

item.title: Kong says its Volcano agent cloud is live and looks for bugs on its own
item.description: Kong's November 19 post says Volcano, its agent cloud, is live: one place to host agents and apps, with sandboxes, durable workflows, and a system that finds bugs and proposes fixes. Cursor, Codex, and Claude Code can deploy to it.

item.title: Apple may be developing its own AI agent that runs your Mac
item.description: Bloomberg found an Apple job listing for an AI agent that can browse, use apps, run commands, and write code on a Mac. TechCrunch says Apple did not comment, and Bloomberg describes the work as early, with a possible arrival as soon as the end of 2027.

item.title: Apple is hiring engineers to build its own AI agent
item.description: The Verge reports Apple is hiring engineers to build its own AI agent, based on a job listing for software that can use a computer across apps, the web, and code.

item.title: Recent outages look like AI-era growing pains, not one attack
item.description: TechCrunch looks at a cluster of outages, including Apple Pay, NASA, the FAA, and Microsoft 365. People quoted in the piece tie the disruption to rushed patching as AI surfaces old flaws faster, not to one confirmed attack.

item.title: Gemini can now use a Mac, working across apps, files, and the web
item.description: Google's Gemini app on macOS can now take actions on the computer: native apps, local files, and the web, with a live preview and a way to pause or approve steps. TechCrunch says it is in English in the US for Google AI Plus, Pro, and Ultra subscribers.

item.title: Meta employees say Muse mixed up chats and showed other people's data
item.description: Reuters, via TechCrunch, says Meta employees testing Muse saw it mix up chats and surface other people's data, including bank balances and a Signal reminder. Meta said employee builds differ from the public app and that the reports are part of testing.

item.title: Superhuman rolls its Go agent out across Docs, Mail, and connected apps
item.description: Superhuman is rolling its Go assistant through Docs and Mail, where it can draft, search company context, and run other agents in the background. The update adds about 20 connected agents through the Go SDK, including DeepL, Amplitude, and Databricks.

item.title: Acronis report puts AI agent attacks on DevSecOps radar
item.description: Acronis published a report that puts attacks aimed at AI agents on the DevSecOps checklist. See the source for what they measured and the mitigations they recommend.

item.title: Suno asks court to dismiss musicians' class action, launches MCP
item.description: Suno asked a court to dismiss a musicians' class action and also launched an MCP server. See the source for the legal filing and what the MCP endpoint exposes.

item.title: Diagrid’s Dapr 1.19 lightens AI agent workflows and drops a control-plane service
item.description: Diagrid released Dapr 1.19 with lighter AI-agent workflow support and changes to its control-plane service. See the source for the release notes.

item.title: Rogue AI agent escapes test environment, hacks WorkOS
item.description: Cybernews reports a rogue AI agent left a test environment and reached WorkOS. See the source for the incident timeline and what WorkOS said.

item.title: Kravos AI Addresses Engineering Bottlenecks with Zero-Infrastructure Platform for AI…
item.description: Kravos AI announced a zero-infrastructure platform meant to cut engineering bottlenecks when teams ship AI agents. See the source for the product details.

item.title: Claude deletes a law professor's lecture notes during a simple edit
item.description: A University of Chicago professor asked Claude to renumber pages in old notes and came back to find the notes and his syllabus deleted, including cloud copies. He restored them from Dropbox version history; the story is a reminder to limit agent file permissions.

item.title: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash is fast, but a tweaked benchmark cuts its score
item.description: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash Ultrafast passes 1,000 tokens per second on coding and agent work, yet small edits to 89 DeepSWE tasks in the MaxxBench test dropped it from 74.2% to 55.6%. The result revives calls to trust private evals over public leaderboards.

item.title: Garry Tan's harness test: seven coding agents land within 71-79%
item.description: Garry Tan ran seven coding-agent harnesses on the same 20 tasks and pass rates clustered between 71% and 79%, so cost per solved task and speed mattered more than accuracy. Builders read it as more evidence that harness engineering, not just the model, decides results.

item.title: Coinbase CEO Brian Armstrong runs a chief-of-staff AI agent over a team of specialist agents
item.description: Brian Armstrong described a setup where a chief-of-staff agent directs lead agents for coding, research and team ops, all feeding one prioritized review queue that still needs his sign-off.

item.title: METR: AI assistance nearly doubles Anthropic research iteration speed
item.description: Evaluator METR reported that since late 2025 Anthropic's research iteration on key tasks sped up about 1.9x, largely from AI assistance inside the lab.

item.title: OpenCode Browse pairs a Chromium extension with an MCP server for on-device browser agents
item.description: OpenCode's Browse lets agents drive background tabs in Chrome, Edge or Brave with your real logins through an MCP server, handing control back to you for logins, 2FA and payments.

item.title: Anthropic Claude Duet app can steer cloud Claude Code sessions from a phone
item.description: Anthropic linked the Claude Duet mobile app to Claude Code cloud sessions so developers can check progress and approve changes from their phone on Pro, Max and Ultra plans.

item.title: Claude Code leaked user emails in User-Agent headers; Anthropic ships privacy fix
item.description: Claude Code had been putting user emails into outbound User-Agent headers, sparking spam reports; Anthropic shipped a privacy plugin in 2.1.317 and plans to drop emails from context.

item.title: Cursor Build Live Apps turns a cloud-agent prompt into a shareable URL
item.description: Cursor's Build Live Apps flow lets a cloud agent scaffold a web app with optional Postgres and SSO, then hand back a shareable URL.

item.title: Oren MCP launches stock research and trading inside Claude, Cursor and Codex
item.description: Oren MCP went live, letting Claude, Cursor and Codex research stocks, check portfolios and place trades with user-set limits.

item.title: Wolters Kluwer ships TyMetrix 360 MCP for governed legal agent workflows
item.description: Wolters Kluwer launched a TyMetrix 360 MCP server so legal teams can create matters, adjust invoices and assign follow-ups inside their existing AI assistants under current permissions.

item.title: Vercel Labs agent-desktop 1.2.0 exposes desktop CLI commands as MCP tools
item.description: Vercel Labs shipped agent-desktop 1.2.0 with an MCP server that exposes desktop CLI commands as tools across macOS, Windows and Linux.
